question: Are goalkeepers and referees separated for the sake of re-ID, and does fixing it move the metrics?
finding: They were not. `tdlp-full` hands detections to an external tracker as MOT and reads MOT back; MOT has no class column, so every tracklet returned as PLAYER however it was detected. That silently disabled the referee exclusion in reid_engine.eligible() and the goalkeeper confidence discount in both team classifiers.

SNMOT-118.wrong_merge_before: entity [10, 30] -> GT tracks {13, 14}, roles {player, referee} — the run's ONLY wrong merge
SNMOT-118.wrong_merge_after: none; the surviving merge [25,27] -> GT track 23 is correct

fixes: matchlab_core/stages/track/_assembly.py::assign_classes_by_overlap — recover a tracklet's class by matching its boxes back to the input detections and taking the majority. Wired into tdlp_full/stage.py behind `recover_detection_class` (default true).

matchlab_core/reid/gates.py::TeamConsistencyGate — takes per-tracklet team confidences and abstains below `team_min_confidence` (default 0.5), so a goalkeeper's halved-confidence guess no longer vetoes a merge.
matchlab_core/stages/track/tdlp/loop.py — the in-repo TDLP tracker hardcoded cls=PLAYER; now majority-votes like iou.py and _assembly.py. NOTE this path is not used by the reid config.
protocol: oracle detect + tdlp-full track + kit-color team + pnlcalib calibrate + reid-engine associate, on SoccerNet SNMOT clips (30 s each). BEFORE arm sets recover_detection_class=false and team_min_confidence=0.0.

SNMOT-123.note: no metric changed; merge_precision was already 1.0 so there was no wrong merge to prevent

SNMOT-125.note: no metric changed; merge_precision was already 1.0

attribution: On SNMOT-118 the three-way split (baseline / +class recovery / +class recovery +goalkeeper gate) shows ALL of the effect comes from class recovery. The goalkeeper gate contributed nothing on any clip measured — it is correct but has not yet been shown to earn its place.
verdict: Improved 2 of 4 clips, unchanged on 2, regressed on 0. Where it fires the win is clean: on SNMOT-120 one wrong merge removed with no correct merge lost (7/9 -> 7/8). Pooled effect is small (+0.005 IDF1) because two clips had no wrong merge to prevent.
caveats: All runs use ORACLE detection, so class labels are perfect. The referee exclusion is a hard gate on a classifier output — the pattern the 2026-07-28 gate-vs-score work concluded is dangerous, since a hard constraint inherits the error rate of whatever estimates it. With a real detector, a player misclassified as a referee is silently dropped from re-ID with no report row. UNMEASURED and the main open risk.
30-second broadcast clips have a far denser referee presence per minute than a full match.
Clips were chosen for having goalkeepers and referees, which biases toward showing an effect (though every SNMOT clip contains both).
n=4 clips; merge_precision on SNMOT-118 is 1-of-1 vs 1-of-2 and is not a meaningful rate.
